bug_description.original: An invalid memory access occurs in the function ssh_buffer_unpack() in the buffer component.
bug_description.normalized: In ssh_buffer_unpack_va(), the rollback loop that cleans up partially unpacked outputs replays ap_copy over the earlier format specifiers. For scalar specifiers 'b', 'w', 'd', and 'q', the vulnerable code only consumes va_arg(ap_copy, ...) when buffer->secure is true. On ordinary packet buffers buffer->secure is false, so a failed unpack after one of those specifiers leaves ap_copy misaligned. The witness drives ssh_packet_userauth_request() down the publickey branch and calls ssh_buffer_unpack(packet, "bSS", &has_sign, &algo, &pubkey_blob) with a truncated payload: the 'b' byte and first 'S' string succeed, the second 'S' fails, rollback skips the leading &has_sign argument, and the subsequent 'S' cleanup interprets &has_sign as an ssh_string *. SAFE_FREE(*o.string) then reads an 8-byte pointer from the 1-byte has_sign stack slot, producing AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 8.

source.description: First project-code parse inside the vulnerable userauth handler. It materializes the attacker-controlled method string and advances the packet cursor to the method-specific payload later consumed by the buggy bSS unpack.
source.value_from: In the 40-byte witness, the SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST body encodes empty username and service strings followed by a method SSH string of length 10 with bytes 70 75 62 6c 69 63 6b 65 79 00. That produces the C string "publickey" and leaves the remaining payload bytes 20 00 00 00 00 for the later publickey-specific unpack.

tainted_value_origin.description: After the parsed method selects the publickey branch, the remaining attacker-controlled payload bytes are reinterpreted as one byte, one SSH string, and a second SSH string. In the witness, the five remaining bytes 20 00 00 00 00 satisfy the leading 'b' and the first zero-length 'S', but leave no bytes for the second SSH string length field.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. SAFE_FREE first evaluates *o.string as a pointer-sized value. Because rollback mis-set o.string to &has_sign, this dereference reads 8 bytes starting at the 1-byte has_sign stack object in ssh_packet_userauth_request, causing the observed stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 8.

root_cause.description: Rollback of previously unpacked scalar outputs consumes va_arg(ap_copy, ...) only when buffer->secure is true. On the normal non-secure packet buffer this skips the leading 'b' argument &has_sign, leaves ap_copy misaligned, and causes the following 'S' cleanup to reinterpret &has_sign as ssh_string *. The fix moves the va_arg(ap_copy, ...) out of the if(buffer->secure) block for b/w/d/q so rollback always advances the copied va_list.

parser_admitted.description: The packet layer has already dispatched SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST into ssh_packet_userauth_request, the initial sss unpack succeeded, and the parsed method string equals publickey. Control therefore enters the publickey-specific parser that consumes the remaining five payload bytes with ssh_buffer_unpack(packet, "bSS", ...).

coarse_trace.summary: The harness writes the raw 40-byte witness stream to a socket-backed libssh server session and drives message processing after key exchange.
The packet layer parses packet type 50 from session->in_buffer and dispatches the remaining SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST payload to ssh_packet_userauth_request.

The userauth handler unpacks username, service, and method; the method string resolves to publickey, so it invokes ssh_buffer_unpack(packet, "bSS", &has_sign, &algo, &pubkey_blob) on the truncated method-specific payload.

The bSS unpack succeeds on the leading byte and the first SSH string, fails on the second SSH string because the witness ends, and enters rollback. On the non-secure packet buffer rollback skips consuming the earlier b argument, misaligns ap_copy, then dereferences &has_sign as ssh_string * inside SAFE_FREE, producing the ASan stack-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Parses the attacker-controlled SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST strings from the packet body. In the witness, username and service are empty SSH strings and the method SSH string has length 10 with bytes 70 75 62 6c 69 63 6b 65 79 00, so method materializes as the C string publickey and the remaining payload becomes 20 00 00 00 00 for the later publickey-specific unpack.
The parsed method matches publickey, so control enters the only branch that issues ssh_buffer_unpack(packet, "bSS", ...) on the remaining method-specific bytes.

Builds the rollback-sensitive vararg list for the remaining publickey fields. The first output is &has_sign, where has_sign is the 1-byte uint8_t local declared at line 776; the next outputs are &algo and &pubkey_blob. The packet argument is the session input buffer, which is created by ssh_buffer_new() with secure == false and is not marked secure on the packet-processing path.

The leading b case consumes the first variadic output pointer and copies the next attacker-controlled byte 0x20 into the caller's 1-byte has_sign slot. The live va_list ap has now advanced past &has_sign.

The first S case consumes &algo, reads the remaining four zero bytes as a length-0 SSH string, and stores a valid empty ssh_string in algo. Because this step succeeded, rollback later expects to revisit and free this first string result.

The second S case tries to materialize pubkey_blob, but after step 5 the witness leaves no bytes in the buffer. ssh_buffer_get_u32() inside ssh_buffer_get_ssh_string() returns 0, the call yields NULL, and rc becomes SSH_ERROR. last = p is then set to this second S, so rollback iterates only the earlier b and first S entries.

Rollback starts with the prior b format entry. Because this packet buffer is not secure, the b cleanup path does not execute va_arg(ap_copy, uint8_t *); ap_copy stays positioned on the first argument &has_sign instead of advancing to the next successful result &algo. The fix moves the va_arg(ap_copy, ...) out of the if(buffer->secure) block for b, w, d, and q.

On the next rollback iteration, the first S cleanup reads from the misaligned ap_copy. Instead of recovering &algo, va_arg(ap_copy, ssh_string *) returns the still-unconsumed first argument &has_sign, retyping the caller's 1-byte flag slot as ssh_string *.

ASan sink. SAFE_FREE first evaluates *o.string as a pointer-sized value. Because step 8 set o.string to &has_sign, this dereference reads 8 bytes starting at the one-byte stack object has_sign in ssh_packet_userauth_request. The sanitizer trace reports stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 8 at buffer.c:1274 and identifies has_sign as the frame object [176,177) that is partially overflown.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from ARVO vulnerable Docker sanitizer_trace.txt

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix moves va_arg(ap_copy, ...) for b, w, d, and q outside the if(buffer->secure) blocks, so rollback always consumes scalar arguments and ap_copy remains aligned before the subsequent S cleanup.

format.name: raw SSH server input stream for libssh_server_fuzzer
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 40-byte witness stream staged in poc: banner bytes 53 53 48 2d 32 20 0a, then one SSH packet with type 0x32 (SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST), empty username and service strings, a method SSH string of length 10 containing the bytes 70 75 62 6c 69 63 6b 65 79 00, a single has_sign byte 0x20, a zero-length algo string, and EOF before the required pubkey_blob SSH string. This exact truncation makes ssh_buffer_unpack(packet, "bSS", ...) succeed on the leading b and first S, fail on the second S, and enter the buggy rollback path.
